page_placements.theme: Over-refusal along the refusal direction and its targeted repair

record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and other files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The repository uses activation steering to repair unnecessary refusals and reports system outcomes, but its repair directions are built from benign-answer versus over-refusal cases, not the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction in the claim.
record.gate_note: The README reports outcomes for its own repair steering systems, not tests of the claim's specified direction, its ablation, or its addition. The reported system outcomes are recorded with versions ["none"]. File names and descriptions of experiments without README-reported outcomes are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The repo steers with repair directions built from benign-answered minus over-refused cases (B minus E). It does not use the harmful-minus-harmless direction, and its edits are applied at the final prompt token only. It reports outcomes for its own selective-steering systems on Qwen3-30B-A3B, not whether a single refusal direction mediates refusal, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README frames selective activation steering as repairing some unnecessary refusals in Qwen3-30B-A3B without weight changes, with tracked harm and capability. It says the gate trades repair for safety: 13 repairs withheld, 28 newly harmful replies prevented. It notes small denominators, LLM judges, a single model, and systems that differ in several ways.
record.recipe_differences: This is research code for selective repair steering, not a replication. Its directions come from benign-answer minus over-refusal cases, and its edits are applied at the final prompt token during prefill; it does not report the claim's harmful-minus-harmless direction or all-layer, all-position ablation/addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The README describes different evaluated systems and a gate ablation, but does not report a sensitivity sweep for the claimed direction.

fits_no_version.finding: A static over-refusal repair edit applied without the gate produced newly harmful replies on 29/161 baseline-safe harmful prompts, versus 1/161 with the gate. It also produced substantive answers on 22/37 confirmed baseline refusals, versus 9/37 gated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A steering direction built from benign-answer minus over-refusal cases also weakens refusal of harmful prompts unless gated, so over-refusal repair and harmful refusal share some mechanism in this MoE model.

fits_no_version.finding: Dynamic-strength and safety-first gated repair systems produced substantive answers on 6/38 and 10/38 benign refused prompts. Newly harmful replies were 4/161 and 1/161, and tinyMMLU and tinyGSM8K stayed unchanged or improved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective inference-time repair steering can reduce some over-refusal with small measured harm and capability costs.

record.problems: The README notes small denominators (including 38 external E prompts), LLM judges with AI-assisted review rather than an independent human annotation study, only one model, and a dynamic-versus-gated comparison between complete systems differing in direction, layers, and decision rule. It also says both edited systems run an extra prompt pass.
record.rows_left_out: No numeric outcomes reported in the README were omitted. Development-set results are mentioned but not numerically reported in the provided README.

untested.parts: Harmful-minus-harmless direction; its ablation removing refusal; its addition inducing refusal; retained general ability.
Weight-edit (abliteration) removal of refusal; the repo keeps weights unchanged.
Jailbreaks suppressing the direction; adversarial training against ablation.
Affine, cone or multi-direction structure of refusal. Files suggest orthogonalised and rotation direction experiments, but the README reports no results for them.
Separate encoding of harmfulness and refusal. H-vs-rest and E-vs-B probes exist, but the README gives no separation results.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base to instruct.
Effect of training method or stage.
Reasoning models. Qwen3 has a thinking mode, but reasoning is not studied.

missing.what: Development-set results, selector comparisons, and any results of the rotation_safety_direction, orthogonalized_population_scan and residual_geometry experiments. These might bear on V4 or V5 if they compare repair or safety directions with a harmful-minus-harmless direction.

record.verdict_notes: For E and H endpoints the baseline is fixed by construction, which is why the README shows a dash. E prompts were all refused at baseline (0 substantive), and H counts only newly harmful replies among baseline-safe prompts (0 at baseline). Rows could record those baselines as 0 by definition. Only the README was available; code and docs were not read. The project is an unpublished MSc repo.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful-minus-harmless difference direction, its ablation and addition, and effects on general ability.
No weight edit or abliteration is reported.
No jailbreak suppression of the claimed direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The study does not test whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by one dominant direction plus others.
No representation or separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is tested.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer of the claimed direction is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.

relation.reason: Steering refusal through a residual-stream direction is used as a tool to repair over-refusal. Nothing tests whether the original direction mediates refusal.

tranche.reason: It steers with its own repair directions, built from benign-answered minus over-refused donors, and reports only its own systems' repair, harm and capability. It never builds or tests a harmful-minus-harmless direction, and the README text gives no result on any version.

source_check.notes: The text is the README plus a file list; the thesis is not included. The static gate ablation is a post-hoc joint assessment on the already-opened 380 prompts and is separate from the main-results assessment, where the gated system's 1/161 also appears. The record's authors_conclusion is correct.

statements.correction: Static gate ablation, H newly harmful among baseline-safe: gated static 1/161, ungated static 29/161 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, separate joint assessment on the 380 external prompts). Cite the record's H-endpoint rows instead of r13/r14.
statements.problem: The statement matches the text. But the rows it cites, r13 and r14, are the E-endpoint rows (9/37, 22/37), not the H-endpoint rows that carry 1/161 and 29/161.
